texts.preamble: Preetam Singh Jadon vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh Thr on 7 July, 2022 Author: Sunita Yadav Bench: Sunita Yadav 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Gwalior Before Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Sunita Yadav On The 7th Of July, 2022 Criminal Revision No. 1092 of 2016 Between:- Preetam Singh Jadon S/O Shri M.S. Rajput Occupation: Business B -5 Basudhra State Bank Colony Jahangirabad Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh) .....Petitioner (Shri Pradeep Katare-Advocate For The Petitioner) And The State Of Madhya Pradesh Thr Ram Singh Khadya Nirikshak Khadya Evam Aushdhi Prashasan Vidisha (Madhya Pradesh) .....Respondents (Shri Lokendra Srivastiva -Public Prosecutor For The Respondent/State) This revision coming on for hearing this day, the court passed the following: Order
texts.facts: The facts in brief to decide the petition are that the complainant/Food Inspector filed a complaint under Sections 2(ix) (G) (J) (K), 7(II), 7(v) read with Section 16(1) (a) (i) (ii) of Prevention of Food Preetam Singh Jadon vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh Thr on 7 July, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174518270/ 1 Adulteration Act, 1954 [in short the Act] alleging that on 26.05.2003 the co- accused Manoj Sahu was found to be in possession of the adulterated and misbranded Thrush Cola, sweetened carbonated beverages, Thrush orange sweetened carbonated beverages and packaged drinking water. As per the allegations in the complaint, the dealer of the said adulterated items is M/s. Jadon & Company and the present petitioner/accused is the proprietor of that company which was selling the above adulterated food.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner argued that the impugned order is perverse and contrary to the settled principles of law. It is further argued that the learned trial Court has rightly discharged the present petitioner as there is no evidence on record to show the involvement of the petitioner in committing the crime. It is further argued that the learned revisional Court has passed the order on the basis of documents which are not admissible in evidence because the original were not filed before the Court below. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent argued that the impugned order is in accordance with law and need not be interfered with. Heard and perused the record. The Apex Court in the case of State of Rajasthan vs. Fatehkaran Mehdu, reported in (2017) 3 SCC 198 has observed that at the stage of framing of a charge, the court is concerned not with proof of allegation, rather it has to focus on material and form an opinion whether there is strong suspicion that accused has committed an offence, which if put to trial, could prove his guilt. Power of quashing criminal proceedings particularly, charge framed in terms of Section 228 Cr.p.C. should be exercised very sparingly and with circumspection and that too in the rarest of rare cases. The same principle has been laid down in the case of P. Vijayan vs. The State of Kerala, 2010 (2) SCC 398.
